newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: DON APARTMENTS OCCUPANCY RISES ABOVE TARGET.
newsitem.headline: DON APARTMENTS OCCUPANCY RISES ABOVE TARGET.

text.p: South Africa's Don Group Ltd said on Friday that bednight occupancies were rising ahead of target, climbing at an average rate of 75 percent a month.

The Don Group, the country's largest operator in the executive self-catering apartment hotel niche, said in a statement that occupancies for October and November had climbed to an average rate of 75 percent each month.
"This is running ahead of the forecast in the group's 1996 annual report of an average 68 percent for the financial year end June 1997," it said.
Chairman Marc Wainer said the better-than-expected occupancies in recent weeks were partly due to a three million rand advertising campaign.

"On the domestic front, there has been a particularly strong response from the corporate market. Awareness of the lower cost for longer stays in top class accommodation among corporate managements locally is reflected...in a significant increase in bookings for the overseas colleagues," Wainer said.

The group's 30 million rand expansion and refurbishment programme was well underway and by June next year would have increased the number of apartment units to 843 in 16 hotels in Johannesburg, Sandton, Pretoria and Cape Town.
Wainer said that the group planned to introduce its own Internet website next year to raise awareness of the self-catering apartment option.
The group's food division had also improved its performance, Wainer said.
